doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Deciding to be a drummer; first teacher in Elkton
summary: Purdie says he chose music as a baby, played tin pots at three and got a toy set at six. His teacher was the Elkton school band drummer, whom he did not want to emulate as a teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You know I’ve met some versatile musicians doing this projects, but you go from Louis Armstrong to James Brown. I think that covers a lot of turf.
Yes it does, it really does.
Was there a point as a young man where you made a conscious decision to be a musician or did it just kind of evolve?
As a young man my decision to be a musician was done as a baby.
Yeah. I was actually playing drums, tin pots, my mother and father, my parents they say at three.

I got my toy set at six. And it was just on from there. Because my teacher happened to be the drummer for the big band in Elkton, Maryland, which is the Cecil County School System. And he was a drummer. And I wanted to be like him. But he was also a teacher. And that’s the one thing I didn’t want to be. Whoa, was I so wrong.
Yeah. He told me that I was going to be a teacher. And I told him I do not wish that on anyone.
Because you saw him in like a school system type of teacher? Or it was a private teacher? Or both?

Both, actually for me. But being a teacher, he said the same things all the time. I mean you couldn’t get around it. He said it day after day, week after week, month after month, year after year.
